texts.li: [old] Word has come from {FACTION}: {A_nameDef}'s {RELATION}, {RELATIVE}, is old now, and alone more than {A_nameDef} likes to think about. {A_nameDef} has asked the council whether to go to {RELATIVE} for the years that are left.

[old] {A_nameDef} has been quiet since the last traders came through. They brought word of {A_possessive} {RELATION} {RELATIVE}, getting old among {FACTION}, and {A_nameDef} has asked the council to decide whether to go.
[child] {A_nameDef}'s child {RELATIVE} is growing up among {FACTION}, without {A_objective}. {A_nameDef} has asked the council whether to go and be a parent there while there's still time.
[child] Every time traders come from {FACTION}, {A_nameDef} asks after {A_possessive} child {RELATIVE}. Now {A_nameDef} has asked the council to let {A_objective} go and live with {RELATIVE}.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} go to {RELATIVE}
li.outcome: The colony saw {A_nameDef} to the gate with a full pack, and {A_nameDef} set off for {FACTION}, to {RELATIVE}, one of their people now.

li.label: Send {COUNT} silver to {RELATIVE} instead
li.outcome: The colony set {COUNT} silver aside for {RELATIVE}, with a long letter from {A_nameDef}, for the next traders bound for {FACTION}. It won't be {A_nameDef}, and {A_nameDef} still misses {RELATIVE}, but it will help.

li.label: Send for {RELATIVE} to come here, with 300 silver for the road
li.outcome: The colony sent word to {FACTION}, and 300 silver for the road, asking {RELATIVE} to come and live here with {A_nameDef}. {FACTION} will miss one of theirs.

li.label: Ask {A_nameDef} to stay
li.outcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to stay, and {A_nameDef} said yes, trusting the council a little less for it. That night {A_nameDef} wrote a long letter to {RELATIVE}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is here again, and {A_nameDef} hardly leaves {X_possessive} side. {A_nameDef} has asked the council a hard question: go with {X_nameDef}, or ask {X_objective} to stay?

[married] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} are married and have lived apart all this time, {X_nameDef} among {FACTION} and {A_nameDef} here. With {X_nameDef} visiting, {A_nameDef} has asked the council to settle where the two of them belong.
[engaged] {A_nameDef} is to marry {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who is visiting now, and they can't both stay where they are. {A_nameDef} has asked the council what it thinks.
[guest] {X_nameDef} has come to stay as a guest, and {A_nameDef} has spent every evening with {X_objective}. {A_nameDef} has asked the council whether to go home with {X_nameDef} to {FACTION}.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes to be with {X_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} packed that same day, and the colony saw {A_objective} to the gate. {A_nameDef} set off ahead for {FACTION}, one of their people now, to be there when {X_nameDef} comes home.

li.label: Ask {X_nameDef} to join the colony
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} said yes before the question was finished, and is one of the colony now. {A_nameDef} hasn't stopped smiling. {FACTION} have lost one of theirs, and think less of the colony for it.

li.label: Things stay as they are
li.outcome: Nothing changes: {X_nameDef} will go home when the visit ends, and come back when {X_pronoun} can. {A_nameDef} took it quietly, and trusts the council a little less.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has slept crowded in with everyone else for too long, and has nobody here of {A_possessive} own to stay for. {A_nameDef} has asked the council to let {A_objective} move on to somewhere with room, unless there's a room to be had here.
Night after night on a bedroll among the others, and {A_nameDef} is worn thin by it. {A_nameDef} came to the council: a room of {A_possessive} own, or leave to go and find one elsewhere.
{A_nameDef} has been miserable for days, sleeping wherever there's space and never alone. With no family or partner here, {A_nameDef} has asked whether the colony still has a place for {A_objective}.

li.label: Promise {A_nameDef} a room of {A_possessive} own
li.outcome: The council promised {A_nameDef} a room of {A_possessive} own. Now the colony has to build it, and soon: a broken promise would cost more than the room.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} move on
li.outcome: The colony saw {A_nameDef} to the gate with food for the road, and {A_nameDef} went to find somewhere with room.

li.label: Ask {A_nameDef} to make do
li.outcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to make do a while longer. {A_nameDef} said yes, and didn't look at anyone.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} kept {A_possessive} word and stayed, but hasn't stopped thinking about {RELATIVE}, {A_possessive} {RELATION} among {FACTION}. {A_nameDef} has come back to the council: let {A_objective} go, or bring {RELATIVE} here.
[old] {RELATIVE} isn't getting any younger, and {A_nameDef} knows it. {A_nameDef} has asked the council a second time to let {A_objective} go to {FACTION}, while there's time.

[child] Every day {A_nameDef} stays, {A_possessive} child {RELATIVE} grows up a little more among {FACTION} without {A_objective}. {A_nameDef} has asked the council again, and this time it isn't really a question.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} go to {RELATIVE}
li.outcome: The colony saw {A_nameDef} to the gate with a full pack, and {A_nameDef} set off for {FACTION}, to {RELATIVE}, one of their people now.

li.label: Send for {RELATIVE} to come here, with {COUNT} silver for the road
li.outcome: The colony sent word to {FACTION}, and {COUNT} silver for the road, asking {RELATIVE} to come and live here with {A_nameDef}. {FACTION} will miss one of theirs.

li.label: Insist that {A_nameDef} stays
li.outcome: The council said no a second time. {A_nameDef} will stay, and won't forget that the council kept {A_objective} from {RELATIVE}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is back, and {A_nameDef} has had enough of goodbyes. {A_nameDef} has come to the council again: go with {X_nameDef}, or have {X_objective} stay for good.

[married] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} are married, and see each other only when {X_nameDef} can get away from {FACTION}. With {X_nameDef} here again, {A_nameDef} has asked the council a second time where the two of them belong.
[guest] {X_nameDef} is a guest here again, and {A_nameDef} can't bear another parting. {A_nameDef} has asked the council once more to let {A_objective} go home with {X_nameDef}.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes to be with {X_nameDef}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} packed that same day, and the colony saw {A_objective} to the gate. {A_nameDef} set off ahead for {FACTION}, one of their people now, to be there when {X_nameDef} comes home.

li.label: Ask {X_nameDef} to join the colony
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} said yes, and is one of the colony now. {A_nameDef} hasn't stopped smiling. {FACTION} have lost one of theirs, and think less of the colony for it.

li.label: Insist that {A_nameDef} stays
li.outcome: The council said no a second time. {X_nameDef} will go home alone when the visit ends, and {A_nameDef} won't forget who kept them apart.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has made do, and made do, and is done with it. {A_nameDef} has asked the council again for a room of {A_possessive} own, or leave to go.
[broken] The council promised {A_nameDef} a room, and {A_nameDef} is still sleeping among the others. {A_nameDef} has come back to the council: a room now, or leave to go.
[noroom] {A_nameDef} is still sleeping crowded in, and nobody here has a room to spare. {A_nameDef} has asked the council a second time to let {A_objective} go.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} move on
li.outcome: The colony saw {A_nameDef} to the gate with food for the road, and {A_nameDef} went to find somewhere with room.

li.label: Give {A_nameDef} someone's room
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} gave up {B_possessive} room to {A_nameDef}, and sleeps where {A_nameDef} slept from tonight.

li.label: Insist that {A_nameDef} stays
li.outcome: The council said no a second time. {A_nameDef} will stay where {A_pronoun} sleeps now, and won't forget it.
